evidence: For large-scale image classification, we adopt ImageNet LSVRC2012 dataset [5] with 1,000 object categories.
we use three popular fine-grained benchmarks, i.e., CUB-200-2011(Birds) [31], FGVC-aircraft (Aircrafts) [27] and Stanford cars (Cars) [17]
We determine the number of iterations N by cross-validation.
We train iSQRT-COV networks from scratch in 60 epochs, initializing the learning rate to 10-1.1
unresolved: n_seeds not stated anywhere; no repetition/trial/seed language found, so left null rather than defaulted to 1.

n_models counted as the 5 backbone architectures evaluated (AlexNet, ResNet-50, ResNet-101, ResNet-152, VGG-D); paper could alternatively be read as evaluating only its own iSQRT-COV method with two pre-normalization variants (trace vs Frobenius) plus a compact-dimension variant.

n_baselines is an approximate count (~14: MPN-COV, B-CNN, DeepO2P, Improved B-CNN, G2DeNet, original AlexNet/ResNet, FBN, SORT, KP, CBP, NetVLAD, LRBP, HIHCA) since different comparison sets appear on the ImageNet table vs the FGVC table and some (e.g. IR_CNN in Table 2a) appear to be alternate implementations of Improved B-CNN rather than fully distinct methods.
control_arm is not a meaningful concept for this vision-architecture paper (no poisoning/attack framing); set to 'none' per the schema's guidance for this paper type.

n_eval_types counted as: (1) top-1/top-5 classification error rate, (2) forward+backward computation time, (3) meta-layer memory usage, (4) fine-grained-benchmark classification accuracy; these could be split more finely.
